Theorem
Source: topping:page-0045, topping:page-0046 1. ch3:1.1\group maximum-principle

Let $g(t)$ and $X(t)$ be smooth time-dependent metrics and vector fields on a closed manifold $\M $, for $t\in [0,T]$ with $0<T<\infty $. Let $F:\RR imes [0,T] o \RR $ be smooth, and suppose $u\in C^\infty (\M imes [0,T],\RR )$ satisfies \[ rac{\partial u}{\partial t} \leq \Delta _{g(t)}u+\langle X(t), abla u angle +F(u,t). \] If $\phi :[0,T] o \RR $ solves \[ egin{cases} \dfrac {d\phi }{dt}=F(\phi (t),t),\ \phi (0)=\alpha \in \RR , \end{cases} \] and $u(\cdot ,0)\leq \alpha $, then $u(\cdot ,t)\leq \phi (t)$ for every $t\in [0,T]$.

Proof

\sketch For $\e >0$, perturb the comparison solution by solving

\[ egin{cases} \dfrac {d\phi _\e }{dt}=F(\phi _\e (t),t)+\e ,\ \phi _\e (0)=\alpha +\e . \end{cases} \]

For sufficiently small $\e $, this solution exists on $[0,T]$ and converges uniformly to $\phi $. If $u<\phi _\e $ first fails at $(x,t_0)$, then $x$ is a spatial maximum at time $t_0$, so $ abla u(x,t_0)=0$, $\Delta u(x,t_0)\leq 0$, and $\partial _tu(x,t_0)-\phi _\e '(t_0)\geq 0$. The differential inequality and the perturbed ODE then imply $0\geq \e >0$, a contradiction. Letting $\e \downarrow 0$ proves the claim.
